doc.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Sitting in with Basie and helping younger players
summary: He recalls sitting in with Basie's band while in the Army and Basie's remark, and says to help those coming up.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It seems like you’ve had some very fortunate working situations throughout your career that really gave you what you needed for the rest of your career.

Yeah. Well I said I’ve been lucky I’ve been able to play with all the people that I used to look up to when I was a teenager. Like I thought Basie was the greatest thing in life and when I was in the Army, one of the bass players in the Army, Walt Yoder had worked with Woody’s band and he knew all the guys in the Basie band and he took me and the guitar player, my best friend Tony Rizzi, out to the ballroom to see Basie, and he arranged for us to sit in. I mean I’m like 20 years old and Basie’s one of my idols, and the only way you can play with Basie’s band is to play like Basie. I don’t care what other style you play. So I just did my Basie bit. I did an intro, you know [scats] and the tenths and all that routine. And Basie, being a very nice guy, I mean I got to know him very well because we did a lot of work with him with Ella, Basie and Ella were together a lot. And I told him about, you know I said when I was a kid and I sat in with your band, you came up to me after the set I played and you said, “hey kid, you trying to take my job?” That’s the nicest thing you could say. I had another experience with a trumpet player who had his own band when I was a kid and I went up on the stage and I said Mr. so-and-so, “how do you pick the guys in your band?” He says, “get away, don’t bother me.” Well this guy ended up sitting in the band in Florida playing trumpet in the band there, and I was conducting for Sammy. I never told him, naturally. It was just the difference. You know I mean that kind of an attitude I really don’t appreciate. Because by your students you will be taught.
